facts: far past its ceiling an account may get before a LIVE session is cut.

The ceiling above gates fresh admission only, a session already open is never interrupted, and for a $15 account that is the right trade: the overshoot is bounded by one ordinary session and interrupting real work to save cents is the worse error. At $0.50 the same rule is not the same rule.
Reasons whose ceiling is small enough that the hard multiplier applies.
True when ipinfo flagged the egress and NO second opinion could be obtained, every configured privacy provider was disabled, exhausted, or erroring.
The spend at which even a LIVE session is refused, or `null` when the winning ceiling is one the hard cap deliberately does not apply to.

entries.summary: Shared/Core changes across 2 file(s) (+103/−0).

ai.title: Hard spend ceiling multiplier and unverified egress paths added
ai.summary: common/src/constants/freebuff-spend-ceilings.ts introduces FREEBUFF_SPEND_CEILING_HARD_MULTIPLIER = 2 and resolveFreebuffHardSpendCeiling, which returns ceiling.usd multiplied by two for reasons in HARD_CAPPED_REASONS (restricted_country, privacy_egress, flagged_email_domain, third_party_client, unverified_egress) and null otherwise, so a LIVE session is refused only when spending reaches ceiling * 2 while fresh admission still stops at the raw ceiling. common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts adds 'skipped' to FreebuffSpurStatus and FreebuffScamalyticsStatus and adds 'unverified_egress_limited' to FreebuffPrivacyDecision, so a provider that was deliberately not consulted (switched off, exhausted, or erroring) now leaves the egress escalation unresolved, which the new resolver reads as the unverified_egress reason tied to the restricted ceiling.
ai.evidence: common/src/constants/freebuff-spend-ceilings.ts adds the exported constant FREEBUFF_SPEND_CEILING_HARD_MULTIPLIER = 2, the HARD_CAPPED_REASONS set, and the exported function resolveFreebuffHardSpendCeiling(ceiling, multiplier) that returns ceiling.usd * multiplier for hard-capped reasons or null otherwise. common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts adds the 'skipped' status to FreebuffSpurStatus and FreebuffScamalyticsStatus and the 'unverified_egress_limited' variant to FreebuffPrivacyDecision.
ai.unknowns: The consuming code that calls resolveFreebuffHardSpendCeiling is not present in this diff, so the rollout of the mid-session hard cut is not visible here.

facts: Names the host, because the overwhelmingly likely cause is an extension or DNS filter blocking it, a cause the user can fix in ten seconds if they know it and cannot fix at all if they do not. Retrying does not help here, so "please try again" alone would be actively misleading.

Google reCAPTCHA site keys, BOTH versions, which run together rather than as alternatives. v3 scores the session invisibly; v2 asks the human to click a box. Public by design; the secret halves are `RECAPTCHA_V2_SECRET_KEY` and `RECAPTCHA_V3_SECRET_KEY`.

entries.summary: Shared/Core changes across 2 file(s) (+58/−1).

ai.title: Add reCAPTCHA env schema and distinct block reasons
ai.summary: Added NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_V2_SITE_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_V3_SITE_KEY, and NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_V2_SIZE to clientEnvSchema. Introduced recaptcha_missing and recaptcha_invalid to SignupBlockReason. These changes separate reCAPTCHA failures from Turnstile 'captcha' errors to aid debugging and support dual-version reCAPTCHA configuration.

eli5.text: If you sign up for an account and it gets blocked, you might now see a message that names Google's reCAPTCHA specifically instead of a generic verification failure, so you can quickly check whether a browser extension or network filter is blocking it. The system now reads new settings that let it use both invisible and click-box versions of Google's reCAPTCHA alongside its existing Turnstile verification, and it keeps reCAPTCHA errors separate from Turnstile errors in its logs for faster troubleshooting. These changes apply to anyone signing up for an account today.

facts: A checkpoint can land after an assistant tool call is recorded but before its result arrives. Drop that half-step at the persistence boundary so a resumed run starts from structurally valid history.
entries.title: SDK update: run
entries.summary: SDK changes across 1 file(s) (+167/−48).

ai.title: SDK run.ts drops unanswered tool calls at persistence boundary
ai.summary: sdk/src/run.ts imports and applies dropUnansweredToolCalls to state.mainAgentState.messageHistory before saving checkpoints. This ensures that assistant tool calls lacking results are removed from the persisted history, preventing structural errors on resume. The change targets the SDK persistence layer to guarantee valid message history for resumed runs.

eli5.text: When you save your progress, the system now quietly removes any tool requests that were started but never finished before writing them to disk. This only affects people resuming a saved session: you won't see half-finished tool calls anymore, and the program won't crash on restart trying to load an incomplete message. From your perspective it just means saves are a little smoother and resumes are a little safer.

ai.title: Add restricted cohort notices and spend notice picker
ai.summary: Added `FREEBUFF_RESTRICTED_NOTICE` refusal copy, `FREEBUFF_RESTRICTED_NOTICE_REASONS` set, and `freebuffSpendNoticeFor` selector to `common/src/constants/freebuff-spend-ceilings.ts`, so restricted cohorts (VPN/proxy egress, restricted country, flagged email domain) receive a more descriptive capacity message instead of the generic `FREEBUFF_CAPACITY_NOTICE`. The notice names the set of causes rather than which signal applied, keeping `third_party_client`, `region`, and `trust_level` on the blind copy on purpose. This follows an explicit 2026-08-14 operator decision to reduce support cost for full-region developers hitting the fifty-cent cap with a message that told them nothing.
ai.evidence: Added export `FREEBUFF_RESTRICTED_NOTICE` string, `FREEBUFF_RESTRICTED_NOTICE_REASONS` ReadonlySet containing 'privacy_egress', 'restricted_country', 'flagged_email_domain', 'unverified_egress', and `freebuffSpendNoticeFor(reason)` function in `common/src/constants/freebuff-spend-ceilings.ts`
ai.unknowns: The specific surfaces in the CLI or web app that consume `freebuffSpendNoticeFor` for display are not visible in the diff.

entries.summary: Shared/Core changes across 1 file(s) (+81/−17).

ai.title: Mainstream privacy mailboxes no longer price the spend ceiling
ai.summary: ProtonMail, Tutanota, Apple Hide-My-Email, DuckDuckGo Email Protection, and Firefox Relay domains are reclassified from `privacy_relay` to a new `mainstream_privacy` category in `common/src/util/disposable-email.ts`, so the spend ceiling now skips them via the freshly exported `isSpendCeilingFlaggedEmailDomain` check that returns false for `mainstream_privacy`. The move is grounded in an operator decision (2026-08-14) that these big-brand consumer mailboxes are a person's primary inbox, not an alias mint, ending two days where they were billed as bot-farm signals. `mainstream_privacy` is still returned by `classifyEmailDomain`, so trust scoring and abuse scripts keep seeing these domains.
ai.evidence: common/src/util/disposable-email.ts: the `mainstream_privacy` variant is added to `FlaggedEmailDomainKind`, ProtonMail/Tutanota/Apple Hide-My-Email/DuckDuckGo/Firefox Relay domains move from `PRIVACY_RELAY_EMAIL_DOMAINS` into a new `MAINSTREAM_PRIVACY_EMAIL_DOMAINS` set, and the new `isSpendCeilingFlaggedEmailDomain` returns false for that kind.
